answer: Each identity locks a 100-credit anchor bond in a public registry, one per record, so no record covers two identities. Auditors wander a route and sign only at a ridge checkpoint; each sighting binds to one record, unreusable. Proving two anchor records share one operator pays 40% of both bonds as bounty. Hiding the k-th fake needs bribing k-1 ridge witnesses at 20 each, so it costs 100+20(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 10,090,000. An honest agent pays one bond, refundable after a clean epoch. A bribed ring fails: only the first reporter is paid, and any auditor on the same wander route can claim it.
